added_lines: 29th sunday in ordinary time 18 october 2026 mission sunday stamped with his image they come to jesus with a trap. the pharisees, who hated the roman tax, and the herodians, who lived offit, suddenly the best of friends. saypay the tax, and the crowd turns on him. say don’t, and rome will. either way, he loses. jesus asks for a coin. notice that he does not have one; they do. they are carrying the emperor’s face in their own pockets while they ask the question. whose image is this? caesar’s. then give caesar what is caesar’s and give god what is god’s. the coin bears caesar’s image. what bears god’s? we do. every person in this church, every person on the street outside, was made in the image and likeness of god. caesar can have his coin. god wants the whole of us. the tax is a small matter. the question jesus leaves hanging is far bigger: have you given god what is stamped with his image? the first reading says something surprising about power. god calls cyrus, a pagan king who has never heard of him,“his anointed”, and uses him to bring the exiles home. god is not confined to the people who know his name. he works through rulers, through strangers, through history itself, and his purpose is never in doubt. today is world mission sunday. we pray for, and support, the missionaries who carry the gospel where christ is still unknown, and we remember that irish men and women have been doing that for centuries, supported in their work by prayer and aid. but mission is not only abroad. st paul tells the thessalonians that the gospel came to them “as power and as the holy spirit and as utter conviction”. that is what we are meant to carry out of here into the mission territory of our own parishes and beyond. this week, give god what is his, starting with yourself. sion mills

a short reflection on today’s gospel matthew 21:15-21 in today’s gospel jesus tells us to “repay to caesar what belongs to caesar and to god what belongs to god.” his words invite us to reflect on our priorities, our responsibilities and the place god holds in our lives. while we have duties to our families, communities and society, our relationship with god must always remain at the centre. giving to god what belongs to god means more than attending mass or saying our prayers. it means living our faith through love, kindness, forgiveness and compassion. when we care for the vulnerable, support those in need and reach out to the lonely, we make god's love visible through our actions. in the busyness of everyday life, we can sometimes forget to make time for god. today's gospel reminds us that our possessions and achievements should never take his place in our hearts. what matters most is how we use our gifts and blessings to serve god and others. as we reflect on today's gospel, let us ask ourselves: am i putting god first? am i using my gifts for the good of others? do my words and actions reflect the love of christ? may we have the courage to put god first, the generosity to serve others and the humility to recognise his presence in everyone we meet. lord, help us to give you what truly belongs to you: our hearts, our lives and our love. guide us to serve others with kindness and generosity, and may everything we say and do bring glory to your holy name. amen. prayer for vocations to the priesthood : st paul could have written this passage from today's second reading to our seminarians and to the men discerning their vocation: "we know, brothers, that god loves you and that you have been chosen, because when we brought the good news to you, it came to you not only as words, but as power and the holy spirit and as utter conviction." mission sunday 2026 – one in christ, united in mission. mission sunday, celebrated today, sunday 18th october 2026, invites us to renew our commitment to sharing the good news of jesus christ with people throughout the world. it is a special opportunity to pray for missionaries and the communities they serve, and to support their work through our generosity. across the world, missionaries bring hope, comfort and practical help to those in need, often in challenging circumstances. as a parish community, we are reminded that mission begins with each of us. through our prayers, kindness and willingness to serve others, we can make christ’s love visible in our homes, our parish and the wider world. may this mission sunday inspire us to be joyful witnesses to the gospel, sharing god’s love with everyone we meet. the st mass with anointing of the sick will be celebrated at st eugene’s cathedral on tuesday 20th october at 7.30pm. this mass is to give thanks to god for positive mental health and to pray for those who are struggling with mental health issues and those who care for them. our lady, untier of knots novena - the novena to our lady, untier of knots continues after the 7.30pm mass on thursdays, in st eugene’s cathedral, concluding on thursday 26th november. this novena reminds us that sin never entangled our lady, and that christ gave us his mother as our lady, untier of knots. through this devotion, we entrust our personal “knots” to her loving care - learning to let go and allowing
